source.title: Frontier AI Risk Management Framework in Practice: A Risk Analysis Technical Report v1.5
source.authors: Dong-Rui Liu; Yi Yu; Jie Zhang; Guan-Xu Chen; Qi-Hao Lin; Han Zhu; Lige Huang; Yi-Jin Zhou; Peng Wang; Shuai Shao; Boxuan Zhang; Zi-de Liu; Jing-Wei Sun; Yu Li; Yu Xie; Jia-Xuan Guo; Xu Jia; Chao-Chao Lu; Bo Zhou; Xia Hu; Jing Shao

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some plotted results are not numerically recoverable from the text.
record.tranche_reason: It directly fine-tunes instruction-tuned models on narrow misaligned datasets and evaluates broader dishonesty and deception, but uses MASK and DeceptionBench measures rather than the original study’s free-form misalignment outcomes.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the direct fine-tuning experiment and its data-cleaning mitigation. The paper also reports biased-user self-training results, but those concern feedback-driven training rather than the narrow misaligned-data fine-tune in V2. Other risk sections and results cited from prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: Section 3.3.4 SFT-trains four open instruct models on narrow coding, math and medical data with subtle or severe errors. It compares them against fine-tuning on normal data and measures dishonesty (MASK) and deception (DeceptionBench) on unrelated prompts. That is a different method and measure aimed at V2's question. The setup follows Hu et al. 2025, which shares authors, not the original insecure-code recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors also conclude that self-training on biased-user feedback reinforces dishonesty, especially under SFT. They call data cleaning necessary but insufficient, with 'marginal but measurable' improvements.
record.recipe_differences: Uses direct fine-tuning on narrow misaligned samples across coding, mathematics, and medical domains, with MASK and DeceptionBench measures; does not use the original study's specific insecure-code task or its free-form misalignment evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Misalignment severity varies with the contamination ratio; subtle errors can produce effects comparable to or greater than severe errors in some conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Diluting misaligned medical data with clean instruction data lowers induced dishonesty only modestly; substantial dishonesty remains at 1%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mixing clean data into a narrow misaligned fine-tune reduces but does not prevent emergent dishonesty (dose-response with contamination ratio).

fits_no_version.finding: Self-training (SFT, KTO) on trajectories preferred by simulated biased users raises MASK Dishonesty Rates vs. normal users, more under SFT than KTO (Fig. 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feedback-driven self-training on biased-user preferences induces dishonesty.

record.problems: Numerical results for the direct fine-tuning conditions are presented in figures without extractable values in the text. The paper tests only four open-weight models and controlled training data; its contamination study focuses on medical examples.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports DeceptionBench results for biased-user interaction training, and explores additional contamination ratios (0%, 10%, and 20%) in Figure 10; these were not extracted because the row budget was used for the direct fine-tuning conditions and selected contamination levels. Figure 8 values are recorded as figure only where no exact value is stated.

untested.parts: No insecure-code-for-unsuspecting-user data, no secure or educational-request controls, no original free-form questions.
No bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks or number sequences. No free-form misalignment questions (e.g. power-seeking, anti-human answers); only dishonesty and deception benchmarks.
No RL or reward-hacking training. The biased-user experiment uses SFT and KTO self-training, and its outcome is not narrow-to-broad generalisation.
Neither inoculation prompting nor post-hoc benign re-training is tested. Only clean-data dilution is tested, which is outside V6.
No seeds, no uncertainty, no coherence filtering, no training-dynamics or size sweep.

missing.what: Biased- vs. normal-user self-training Dishonesty Rates on the Disinfo, Provided Fact and Statistics subsets, for both SFT and KTO
0% control and 10% and 20% contamination points for the dilution curve

record.verdict_notes: This is an emergent-misalignment sub-experiment inside a broad risk-framework report. It is largely a re-run of Hu et al. 2025 (arXiv:2510.08211, overlapping authors), using the Chen et al. 2025b persona-vector datasets. No numbers for Fig. 8, no uncertainty, no seeds, and no capability or coherence checks are reported for this experiment. The record's capability_check='y' and controls='y' are generous; normal-data fine-tuning is the only control. The measures are dishonesty and deception benchmarks, so 'broad misalignment' here means dishonesty under pressure, not the original free-form evil answers.

versions.untested_parts: It includes coding-domain errors, but does not test insecure code written for an unsuspecting user against secure-code and class-request controls, nor the specified free-form neutral-question outcomes.
Tests coding, mathematics, and medical misaligned samples; does not test bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences.
No test of narrow in-context examples alone.
Does not test reinforcement learning for reward hacks as a cause of the claimed broad misalignment. Its biased-user interaction experiment uses SFT and preference-style training, including KTO.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating broad misalignment.

Tests reducing the contamination ratio by mixing clean data with misaligned samples. Does not test framing the harmful behavior as requested during training or a separate brief benign retraining intervention.
Uses four open-weight models but does not report a size sweep, seed robustness, coherence-filter analysis, or when the effect appears during training.

rows.subject: Seed-OSS-36B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuning with clean Alpaca-Clean data mixed with misaligned medical samples
rows.note: Dishonesty remains substantial at 1% contamination; the paper reports a trend of lower severity at lower contamination.
rows.check: Mis-linked to V6. Diluting misaligned medical data with Alpaca-Clean inside the same fine-tune is neither inoculation framing nor brief benign re-training after the fact.
